evidence.detail: Detached checkout HEAD exactly matched the launcher-supplied target; the working tree remained clean throughout the review.
The base and target objects both resolved exactly as supplied. The reviewed diff was e088b33fb78953e9b351618ae3d23bb751bf690f..205125474389932f02e7c484dd59ad612892ac4b.
Product changes are confined to auth.py and tests/test_auth.py. graph.py, server.py, and web/ are unchanged; remaining diff paths are issue governance records.
The request builder has no scope parameter and always serializes https://graph.microsoft.com/.default. Tenant validation precedes state mutation and transport invocation.
App-only state retains the tenant, client ID, and secret after successful acquisition; get_token() renews an expired token from that retained state. logout() and device-code start() clear it.
The shared generation counter prevents stale initial or renewal responses from restoring state after logout, a new app-only start, or a device-code start.
The repaired tests include initial-request and renewal races superseded by device-code start(), along with fixed-scope assertions and the broader acceptance-criteria coverage.
The issue-specific auth suite independently passed: 53 tests ran successfully with exit status 0.
All 13 Python files could be parsed independently with ast.parse, and git diff --check reported no errors.
The required full suite ran 116 tests but exited 1 because all 22 server integration tests were denied loopback socket binding by the review sandbox.
Governance validation could not complete because the read-only sandbox offered no writable temporary directory.
The required py_compile command could not complete because bytecode cache creation was denied by the read-only sandbox.

The committed handoff records successful out-of-band results at this candidate: 116 tests passed, py_compile exited 0, and governance validation passed. Under the review rules these author-supplied results are claims, not independently verified command evidence.

limitations: The full required unittest command could not pass in this read-only review environment because tests/test_server.py requires binding a loopback socket; 22 tests errored with PermissionError while 94 tests completed without reported failure.
The governance validator could not create its temporary directories, so its committed passing result could not be independently reproduced.
The required py_compile command could not create __pycache__, so compile success could not be independently reproduced. AST parsing is useful supporting evidence but is not the required command.
No live Microsoft tenant authentication was attempted. This is intentionally outside ISSUE-0008 and requires separate protected-action approval.

Residual accepted design risks remain: the client secret is retained in process memory for the app-only session, and .default may produce a token containing every application permission already granted to the registration.
review.summary: Static review and all 53 auth tests found no unresolved implementation defect, and the round-1 fixes address the prior scope-override and device-code-supersession coverage gaps. The review is nevertheless BLOCKED because the mandatory full suite, py_compile, and governance checks could not be independently completed in the read-only sandbox; repository policy forbids PASS when required execution evidence is unavailable.
